synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Waiting for consent, not chair time, dominates the pathway from screening to treatment, and a combined consent form raised return in comparison schools. Lean redesign of the clinic day raised chair utilisation in eight schools. SDF itself arrests most lesions, but staining on front teeth is acceptable to fewer than a third of parents, who want to see a photograph first. Families with limited majority-language proficiency return fewer forms, and bilingual calls help more than translation. Teachers support clinics but want predictable timing. The evidence supports a lean redesign focused on consent and flow, judged separately by numbers and by the views of families and staff.
gradeRationale: Before-after reports, non-random comparisons and qualitative studies with selected participants; consistent on where the delays are, imprecise on effect sizes.
summary: Eight records appraised; five source-derived claims; certainty low.
